body:
Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/392
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Define a companion **connector contract** for work trackers and forges, so post-merge workflows can read context and write outcomes without being tied to one vendor.

## Requested capability

**Read**
- A merged change request: identity, merge and base commits, changed files with status, author, and timestamps.
- A work item and its full parent chain up to a configured hierarchy level (for example, walking `parent` until reaching the epic level). The connector returns raw content only to the intake step (see the intake request).

**Write**, performed only by deterministic steps and never by an agent tool call
- **Upsert a follow-up work item.** Look it up by a stable key, such as a label derived from the merged change. Create it or update it. Set its parent to the resolved hierarchy item and link it to the source item. The body is rendered from a fixed template that interpolates only identifiers, enums, paths, URLs, and counts. Include a no-op rule, so changes with nothing to do create no item.
- **File findings.** File them against policy gates: an allowlist of classes, a per-change cap, a requirement that the cited path and line exist at the merge commit, and a rule that security-shaped findings are routed to restricted triage. Filing must be idempotent.
- **Open or update a draft change request** on a branch derived from the stable key, with a generated body.

**Client modes:** `live`, `recording` (writes the requests to a JSONL file), and `dry-run` (prints them). This lets whole workflows be tested without credentials.

**Credentials:** each connector declares the minimum scopes it needs. The contract states that credentials are available only to the writing step.

## Acceptance

- The contract, a conformance kit, and at least two reference connectors of different kinds are published.
- Running the same upsert twice yields one item.
- The recording mode's output is stable across runs.
- Tests show that a rendered body cannot contain strings outside the whitelist.

## Why

Every adopter currently writes this glue by hand: tracker field discovery, lookup by label, parent linking, and caps on findings. Without a contract, the parts that matter for safety (idempotency, a text whitelist, credential separation) are reinvented for each project.


Part of #388.
title: GH #392: Feature: work-tracker and forge connector contract (read hierarchy, idempotent follow-up item, gated findings, draft change requests)
